title: JPMorgan CEO sends blunt warning on 'rogue' AI agents
key_facts: Jamie Dimon, JPMorgan Chase chief executive, spoke on the third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday 13 October.
He said the bank will not allow unvetted outside AI agents into its systems.
He said 'You don't want rogue agents, and there could be thousands of them'.
A JPMorgan spokeswoman told CNBC outside agents cannot act for a customer or log in with their credentials.
Outside agents can view balances read-only if the customer authorises a connector like Plaid; they cannot send money or pay bills.
The bank gave no timeline for changing that; it already runs AI agents internally and plans customer-facing ones.
quote_evidence: "You don't want rogue agents, and there could be thousands of them," he added, according to the transcript.
People who use outside agents should understand the risk and "the liability transfer," he said on the call, adding that the bank is building tools to protect customers.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows where a big bank draws the line on third-party AI agents handling customer accounts.
